newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded sharply higher on light to moderate demand and offerings, USDA said.
Retail demand was for immediate needs at these sharply higher price levels, experienced during this trading period.

Chuck and round cuts traded at higher price levels throughout the week, again most retailers were trying to fill just their immediate needs on light offerings, consequently some round cuts experienced a ten to fifteen dollar increase. Loin and rib cuts traded sharply higher on most cuts, except the tenderloins which remain generally steady.

The Select rib and loin cuts experienced the strongest gains during the week, while some Choice cuts were rather uneven. The closely trimmed product followed the same pattern as the commodity product, traded sharply higher on light to moderate demand. Beef trimmings traded sharply higher for the week, even with the light demand at the beginning of the week and continued as the week progressed.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded higher on light to moderate demand and light offerings with the fed cattle coarse ground items experiencing the biggest gains for the week.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 6.00 to 7.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 2.50 to 4.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 4.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 8.00 to 11.00 higher; Closely trimmed item's 5.00 to 6.00 higher; Beef trimmings 6.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 2.50 to 6.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 5.16 at 103.40; 700/850 Up 5.67 at 103.79; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 5.05 at 98.47; 700/850 Up 4.93 at 97.94.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT After many weeks of downward momentums the boneless beef market turned upward and finished the week sharply higher. The increase seen this week in the lean boneless beef complex was the largest ever. This resulted from good to very good demand and light offerings.

Cow slaughter numbers continued to be light causing supplies and offering to be limited. In return the cow carcasses market also traded sharply higher on moderate demand. However, the cow cuts market traded generally steady to firm.
Utility carcasses 3.00-6.00 higher; Cutter not established; 90% boneless beef 11.00-12.00 higher in the Midwest, Texas 16.00-17.00; 85% 13.00-14.00 higher; 75% 3.00-9.00 higher; 65% 9.00 higher.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, June 19, 1997 was estimated at 81.97 per cwt., up 7.32 from a week ago Friday.
